In [[category theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], a '''power object''' in a category is an analogue of a [[powerset]] in the category of sets.

== Definition ==

Let <math>\mathcal{C}</math> be a [[finitely complete category]]. A ''power object'' of <math>A \in \mathcal{C}</math> is an object <math>\mathcal{P}(A)</math> together with a [[subobject]] <math>(\in) \hookrightarrow A \times \mathcal{P}(A)</math> satisfying the following [[universal property]]: for every other object <math>B \in \mathcal{C}</math> and subobject <math>R \hookrightarrow B \times A</math>, there exists a unique morphism <math>\chi : B \to \mathcal{P}(A)</math> such that <math>R \hookrightarrow B \times A</math> is the pullback of <math>(\in) \hookrightarrow A \times \mathcal{P}(A)</math> along <math>\chi</math>.{{sfn|Johnstone|2002|p=69}}

== Properties ==

In the [[category of sets]], power objects exist: <math>\mathcal{P}(A)</math> is the usual power set of <math>A</math>, and <math>(\in) \hookrightarrow A \times \mathcal{P}(A)</math> is the set membership relation.

More generally, in any [[elementary topos]], the power object of <math>A</math> can be constructed as <math>\mathcal{P}(A) := \Omega^A</math> (where <math>\Omega</math> is the [[subobject classifier]]), with <math>(\in) \hookrightarrow A \times \Omega^A</math> being the subobject classified by the [[Evaluation map (category theory)|evaluation map]] <math>A \times \Omega^A \to \Omega</math>.{{sfn|Johnstone|2002|p=68}}

Conversely, every finitely complete category with power objects is an elementary topos.{{sfn|Johnstone|2002|p=92}} Thus, power objects provide a possible simplification of the definition of an elementary topos.
